# isRegExp

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a regular expression.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isRegExp() — Checks whether a value is a regular expression. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isRegExp(value: unknown): value is RegExp;
```

Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a regular expression; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `RegExp` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isRegExp(/a/); // => true
isRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // => true
isRegExp("/a/"); // => false
isRegExp({}); // => false
isRegExp(null); // => false
```
